title.en: Modu Chanyu Campaigns West Against the Yuezhi

summary.en: After the Han‑Xiongnu heqin settlement, Modu Chanyu concentrated his forces and attacked the Yuezhi tribes in the Hexi Corridor. The Yuezhi were defeated and most migrated west to the Ili River valley (becoming the Greater Yuezhi), while a small remnant stayed near the Qilian Mountains (Lesser Yuezhi). This victory gave the Xiongnu full control of the Hexi Corridor, cutting Han

statement.zh: 冒顿单于在汉匈和亲后，集中主力向西进攻河西走廊的月氏部落。月氏战败后大部分西迁至伊犁河流域（后被称为大月氏），少数留在祁连山一带（小月氏）。此役使匈奴完全控制河西走廊，切断汉朝与西域联系，同时获得月氏的精良战马和冶金技术，匈奴国力达到极盛。
statement.en:
After the Han‑Xiongnu heqin settlement, Modu Chanyu concentrated his forces and attacked the Yuezhi tribes in the Hexi Corridor. The Yuezhi were defeated and most migrated west to the Ili River valley (becoming the Greater Yuezhi), while a small remnant stayed near the Qilian Mountains (Lesser Yuezhi). This victory gave the Xiongnu full control of the Hexi Corridor, cutting Han communication with the Western Regions, and also provided fine warhorses and metallurgical technology from the Yuezhi. Xiongnu power reached its zenith.

For Asia in 199 BCE, “Modu Chanyu Campaigns West Against the Yuezhi” is a traceable node of Military change whose significance is best read through later events.

title.en: Rome Captures Key Cities in the Second Macedonian War

statement.zh: 刘邦遣刘敬送宗室女（称长公主）至匈奴，与冒顿单于结为婚姻。双方约定：以长城为界，北面游牧归匈奴，南面耕织归汉朝；汉朝每年馈赠匈奴絮、缯、酒、米等物资；双方互通关市，减少边境军事冲突。这是汉朝第一次大规模向匈奴输送财物的正式和亲，之后十余年间边境相对平静。
statement.en:
Liu Bang sent Liu Jing to the Xiongnu with a daughter of the clan (styled as a princess) to marry Modu Chanyu. The treaty stipulated: the Great Wall as border, north for nomads and south for farmers; annual Han gifts of silk, wine, grain; and open border markets. This was the first large‑scale shipment of goods by the Han to the Xiongnu. For the next decade, the border was relatively peaceful.

statement.zh: 秦将赵佗在南海郡乘中原战乱之机，击并桂林、象郡，自立为南越武王，定都番禺（今广州）。刘邦派陆贾出使南越，封赵佗为南越王，使其臣属汉朝。赵佗推行“和辑百越”政策，融合汉族与越族文化，南越国在岭南维持近百年统治。
statement.en:
Zhao Tuo, a former Qin general in the Nanhai commandery, took advantage of the chaos in central China to annex Guilin and Xiang commanderies and declared himself King of Nanyue (King Wu ), with his capital at Panyu (modern Guangzhou). Liu Bang sent Lu Jia to Nanyue, formally recognizing Zhao Tuo as king and making Nanyue a nominal vassal. Zhao Tuo pursued a policy of 'harmonizing the Yue peoples', blending Han and Yue cultures. Nanyue would survive for nearly a century.

title.en: Flamininus Proclaims Greek Freedom at Isthmian Games

summary.en: The Roman commander Titus Quinctius Flamininus proclaimed the freedom of the Greek city‑states from Macedonian rule at the Isthmian Games in Corinth. Roman garrisons were withdrawn from most major Greek cities, though some remained. This declaration won Greek sympathy but also gave Rome a pretext to intervene in Greek affairs, beginning the gradual Roman absorption of Greece.

title.en: The Rosetta Stone Inscribed

summary.en: Egyptian priests of Ptolemy V (reigned 204–181 BCE) had the Rosetta Stone carved to honor the king's coronation. At this time Ptolemaic Egypt was declining and relied on priestly support.

summary.en: The conspiracy of Han Xin with Chen Xi was exposed. statement.zh: 淮阴侯韩信与陈豨密谋造反，事泄。吕后与萧何设计，谎称刘邦已平叛归来，将韩信诱至长乐宫钟室斩杀，并诛灭三族。韩信临死感叹“不用蒯通之计，乃为儿女子所诈”。韩信之死标志汉初最杰出的军事家落幕，也显示了吕后果断狠辣的政治手段。
statement.en:
The conspiracy of Han Xin with Chen Xi was exposed. Empress Lü and Xiao He tricked Han Xin into coming to Changle Palace on the pretext that Gaozu had returned victoriously; there he was killed in the Bell Chamber, and his three clans were exterminated. His last words: 'I didn't follow Kuai Tong's advice, and now I die at the hands of a woman.' Han Xin's death marked the end of the most brilliant military commander of the early Han and demonstrated Empress Lü's ruthless political skill.

title.en: Death of Emperor Gaozu of Han

summary.en: Liu Bang was wounded by a stray arrow while suppressing Ying Bu's rebellion. He fell ill on the return march and died in April at Changle Palace in Chang'an, aged 62. His son Liu Ying (Emperor Hui) succeeded, but real power fell to Empress Lü. On his deathbed, Liu Bang had proclaimed the 'Oath of the White Horse', forbidding enfeoffment of non‑Liu as kings. Nevertheless, after

statement.zh: 刘邦在讨伐英布叛乱时被流矢所伤，班师途中病重，四月于长安长乐宫去世，终年62岁。太子刘盈即位为汉惠帝，但实际大权掌握在吕后手中。刘邦临终前留下“白马之盟”，规定非刘氏不得封王，试图防止异姓篡权，但其死后吕后仍大封吕氏子弟为王。
statement.en:
Liu Bang was wounded by a stray arrow while suppressing Ying Bu's rebellion. He fell ill on the return march and died in April at Changle Palace in Chang'an, aged 62. His son Liu Ying (Emperor Hui) succeeded, but real power fell to Empress Lü. On his deathbed, Liu Bang had proclaimed the 'Oath of the White Horse', forbidding enfeoffment of non‑Liu as kings. Nevertheless, after his death, Empress Lü still enfeoffed her own clan members as kings.

For Asia in 195 BCE, “Death of Emperor Gaozu of Han” is a traceable node of Politics change whose significance is best read through later events.

title.en: Rome vs. Seleucid Empire: Battle of Thermopylae

summary.en: Seleucid king Antiochus III entered Greece at the invitation of the Aetolian League. Rome responded with a force that met Antiochus at Thermopylae. The Roman legions defeated Antiochus’s cavalry and elephants, forcing him back to Asia Minor. statement.zh: 塞琉古国王安条克三世应埃托利亚同盟邀请进入希腊，罗马派军阻击。双方在温泉关（德摩比利）激战，罗马军团击败安条克的骑兵和战象，迫使其退回小亚细亚。此战为罗马进军亚洲扫清障碍，安条克三世逃往萨迪斯，次年罗马海军取得决定性胜利。
statement.en:
Seleucid king Antiochus III entered Greece at the invitation of the Aetolian League. Rome responded with a force that met Antiochus at Thermopylae. The Roman legions defeated Antiochus’s cavalry and elephants, forcing him back to Asia Minor. This cleared the way for Rome to march into Asia; Antiochus fled to Sardis, and the following year the Roman navy achieved a decisive victory.

For Europe in 194 BCE, “Rome vs. Seleucid Empire: Battle of Thermopylae” is a traceable node of Military change whose significance is best read through later events.

title.en: Rome Establishes Provincial Administration in Spain

summary.en: The Senate divided Hispania into two provinces, Nearer and Further Spain, each governed by a praetor. Rome had already conquered Carthaginian territories in Iberia, but the local Celtiberian tribes continued to resist. Rome began building roads, establishing colonies, and introducing Latin language and Roman law, gradually Romanizing Spain.

statement.zh: 西汉开国功臣张良病逝。张良出身韩国贵族，曾刺杀秦始皇失败，后辅佐刘邦平定天下，被刘邦赞为“运筹帷幄之中，决胜1000里之外”。晚年他信奉黄老之术，闭关辟谷，得以善终。他的去世使吕后少了一位能够制衡朝局的智囊。
statement.en:
Zhang Liang, a key founding contributor to the Han dynasty, died of illness. Descended from the noble house of the Warring States state of Han, he had failed to assassinate Qin Shi Huang but later helped Liu Bang unify the realm. Liu Bang praised him as 'a strategist who wins battles a thousand miles away.' In his later years Zhang Liang practiced Daoist meditation and fasting, and thus ended his days peacefully. His death deprived Empress Lü of an important counterweight in court.

title.en: Roman‑Seleucid War Erupts

summary.en: The formal war over Greek spheres of influence began between Antiochus III and Rome. Antiochus crossed the Dardanelles into Thrace, attempting to recover Seleucid control over European territory. The Roman Senate declared war, allied with Pergamon and Rhodes, and sent a fleet and army under Lucius Scipio (brother of Scipio Africanus). This war is known as the Syrian War.

title.en: Emperor Hui of Han Dies

summary.en: Emperor Hui, only 24 years old, fell ill and died from depression after witnessing Empress Lü poison his brother Prince Ruyi of Zhao and turn Lady Qi into a 'human pig.' statement.zh: 年仅24岁的汉惠帝因目睹吕后毒杀赵王如意并将戚夫人做成人彘，惊吓成疾，抑郁而终。惠帝死后，吕后立年幼的前少帝刘恭（宫女所生，杀母伪装皇后子），自己临朝称制，成为中国历史上第一位实际执政的皇太后。吕后大封吕氏子弟为王，打破刘邦“非刘不王”的约定。
statement.en:
Emperor Hui, only 24 years old, fell ill and died from depression after witnessing Empress Lü poison his brother Prince Ruyi of Zhao and turn Lady Qi into a 'human pig.' After his death, Empress Lü placed a young child (the former emperor Liu Gong, born of a palace maid and passed off as the empress's son) on the throne as the 'Former Shao Emperor,' and ruled as regent — the first time a Chinese empress dowager effectively governed. She proceeded to enfeoff numerous Lü clan members as kings, breaking Liu Bang's oath.

For Asia in 188 BCE, “Emperor Hui of Han Dies” is a traceable node of Politics change whose significance is best read through later events.

title.en: Antiochus III Dies; Seleucus IV Succeeds

summary.en: Antiochus III was killed (or fell) while plundering a temple. His son Seleucus IV Philopator succeeded. The imperial treasury was exhausted by war indemnities; Seleucus sent his minister Heliodorus to rob the Jerusalem Temple, triggering a revolt in Judaea. The empire fell into financial crisis and internal turmoil.

Antiochus III was killed (or fell) while plundering a temple. His son Seleucus IV Philopator succeeded. The imperial treasury was exhausted by war indemnities; Seleucus sent his minister Heliodorus to rob the Jerusalem Temple, triggering a revolt in Judaea. The empire fell into financial crisis and internal turmoil.

statement.zh: 孔雀王朝末代国王布里哈德拉塔被将军普希亚密特拉·巽伽在阅兵时刺杀。普希亚密特拉建立巽伽王朝（前185-前73年），定都华氏城。新王朝信奉婆罗门教，迫害佛教徒，复兴吠陀祭祀。但疆域仅限于恒河流域，孔雀帝国鼎盛时期的德干高原和西北部已分裂。
statement.en:
The last Mauryan emperor, Brihadratha, was assassinated by his general Pushyamitra Shunga during a military parade. Pushyamitra established the Shunga dynasty (c. 185–73 BCE), with its capital at Pataliputra. The new dynasty favored Brahmanism, persecuted Buddhists, and revived Vedic sacrifices. However, its territory was limited to the Ganges valley; the Deccan and northwest had broken away from the Mauryan empire.

title.en: Empress Lü Deposes and Secretly Kills Former Shao Emperor

summary.en: When the former Shao Emperor Liu Gong learned the truth about his birth mother's murder, he angrily said, 'How could the Empress Dowager kill my mother and still call me her son? statement.zh: 前少帝刘恭长大得知自己生母被杀真相，愤言“太后安能杀吾母而名我？我壮，必为变化”。吕后闻讯将其囚禁永巷，不久废黜并暗中处死，改立常山王刘弘为帝（后少帝）。吕后进一步加强戒备，严密控制宫禁。
statement.en:
When the former Shao Emperor Liu Gong learned the truth about his birth mother's murder, he angrily said, 'How could the Empress Dowager kill my mother and still call me her son? When I am grown, I will take action.' Empress Lü had him imprisoned in the Yong Alley, soon deposed him, and secretly killed him. She then installed Liu Hong, Prince of Changshan, as the Later Shao Emperor, further tightening her control over the palace.

title.en: Death of Scipio Africanus

summary.en: Publius Cornelius Scipio Africanus (Scipio Africanus), the Roman general who defeated Hannibal at Zama, died at his estate in Campania at about age 52. title.en: Hannibal Commits Suicide

summary.en: Hunted by the Romans, the exiled Hannibal took refuge with King Prusias I of Bithynia. When Roman envoys demanded his surrender, Hannibal found himself surrounded and poisoned himself (with poison he kept in a ring), at age 64. statement.zh: 洛阳人贾谊出生，后成为西汉著名政论家、文学家。他少年成名，二十余岁被汉文帝召为博士，撰《过秦论》《治安策》《论积贮疏》，深刻分析秦朝灭亡教训，主张削弱诸侯王、重视农业、改革礼制。其思想对文景之治产生深远影响。
statement.en:
Jia Yi, a native of Luoyang, was born. He would become a famous political commentator and writer of the Western Han. A prodigy, he was summoned to court as an erudite (boshi) in his twenties by Emperor Wen. He wrote 'The Faults of Qin,' 'On the Security of the State,' and 'On Storing Grain,' analyzing the fall of Qin, urging reduction of feudal princes, emphasis on agriculture, and ritual reform. His ideas profoundly influenced the 'Rule of Wen and Jing'.

For Asia in 182 BCE, “Birth of Jia Yi” is a traceable node of Figure change whose significance is best read through later events.

title.en: Rome Divides Macedon into Four Republics

summary.en: The Roman Senate divided the kingdom of Macedon into four autonomous regions, each with its own assembly and treasury. They were forbidden from intermarriage, land ownership across regions, mining silver, or building ships. This dismantled Macedon's military and economic potential, reducing it to a Roman dependency. The four‑region system lasted until Macedon became a province

statement.zh: 罗马元老院将马其顿王国划分为四个自治区域，每个区域建立自己的议会和财政，彼此不得通婚和置产，禁止开采银矿和造船。此举彻底瓦解马其顿的军事和经济潜力，使之沦为罗马附庸。四分区制维持至前146年马其顿正式成为行省。
statement.en:
The Roman Senate divided the kingdom of Macedon into four autonomous regions, each with its own assembly and treasury. They were forbidden from intermarriage, land ownership across regions, mining silver, or building ships. This dismantled Macedon's military and economic potential, reducing it to a Roman dependency. The four‑region system lasted until Macedon became a province in 146 BCE.

For Europe in 181 BCE, “Rome Divides Macedon into Four Republics” is a traceable node of Politics change whose significance is best read through later events.

title.en: Emperor Wen of Han Ascends, Initiating the Rule of Wen and Jing

summary.en: Liu Heng, Prince of Dai, ascended the throne as Emperor Wen of Han. He pursued a policy of letting the people rest: abolishing corporal punishment, reducing land tax (to one‑thirtieth), reducing corvée labor, and opening mountain and marshlands. statement.en:
Liu Heng, Prince of Dai, ascended the throne as Emperor Wen of Han. He pursued a policy of letting the people rest: abolishing corporal punishment, reducing land tax (to one‑thirtieth), reducing corvée labor, and opening mountain and marshlands. He also curtailed powerful families and weakened vassal kings, following Jia Yi's advice to 'divide the large kingdoms into smaller pieces.' Emperor Wen lived frugally, and his reign, together with that of his son Jing, became the first golden age of the Western Han, known as the 'Rule of Wen and Jing.'

title.en: Emperor Wen Abolishes the Crime of 'Sedition'

summary.en: On Jia Yi's advice, Emperor Wen abolished the Qin‑era crime of 'vilification and sedition,' allowing people to criticize the government directly. statement.zh: 文帝采纳贾谊建议，下令废除秦朝以来的“诽谤妖言罪”，允许百姓直言批评朝政。诏书称：“今法有诽谤妖言之罪，是使众臣不敢尽情，而上无由闻过失也。”此举大大活跃了思想，朝中大臣敢于进谏，民间文学也开始复苏，为后世“文景之治”奠定政治宽松的基础。
statement.en:
On Jia Yi's advice, Emperor Wen abolished the Qin‑era crime of 'vilification and sedition,' allowing people to criticize the government directly. His edict stated: 'Now the law has the crime of sedition, which prevents officials from speaking their minds and the ruler from hearing of his mistakes.' This greatly enlivened intellectual life, encouraged officials to remonstrate, and revived folk literature, laying a foundation for political openness during the 'Rule of Wen and Jing.'

title.en: Hellenistic Medicine: Erasistratus Founds Physiological School

summary.en: The famous Hellenistic physician Erasistratus (c. 304–c. 250 BCE) practiced in Alexandria. statement.en:
The famous Hellenistic physician Erasistratus (c. 304–c. 250 BCE) practiced in Alexandria. Through human dissection he discovered that the heart is the center of blood circulation, distinguished sensory from motor nerves, and proposed that air enters the heart via the lungs to form 'vital spirit.' Although his theories had errors, he pioneered systematic anatomy and physiology, influencing the Roman physician Galen.

For Africa in 175 BCE, “Hellenistic Medicine: Erasistratus Founds Physiological School” is a traceable node of Technology change whose significance is best read through later events.

title.en: Rome Expels Epicurean Philosophers

summary.en: The Roman Senate ordered the expulsion of Epicurean philosophers on the grounds that they 'corrupted youth.' The Epicurean school advocated the pursuit of pleasure (in a rational, moderate way) and avoidance of politics—values the conservative Senate saw as corrosive to traditional Roman virtue. Meanwhile, Stoic philosophy continued to spread in Rome and was welcomed by the upp

statement.zh: 罗马元老院以“败坏青年道德”为由，下令驱逐伊壁鸠鲁学派哲学家。该学派主张追求快乐（理性节制）、避免政治参与，被保守的元老院视为对传统罗马美德的腐蚀。但斯多葛学派哲学继续在罗马传播，受到上层欢迎。
statement.en:
The Roman Senate ordered the expulsion of Epicurean philosophers on the grounds that they 'corrupted youth.' The Epicurean school advocated the pursuit of pleasure (in a rational, moderate way) and avoidance of politics—values the conservative Senate saw as corrosive to traditional Roman virtue. Meanwhile, Stoic philosophy continued to spread in Rome and was welcomed by the upper class.

For Europe in 173 BCE, “Rome Expels Epicurean Philosophers” is a traceable node of Culture change whose significance is best read through later events.

title.en: Rome Establishes a Permanent Praetor for Hispania

summary.en: The Senate appointed a special praetor (proconsul) to reside permanently in Hispania, responsible for justice and administration. Previously, the Spanish provinces had been governed by annually rotating consuls or praetors, which was inefficient. This step advanced the maturation of the Roman provincial system, though local tribal resistance remained frequent.

title.en: Roman Consul Paullus Prepares for Decisive Battle

summary.en: The newly appointed consul Lucius Aemilius Paullus arrived in Greece, reorganized the Roman army, and adopted new tactics: dividing the legions into three lines (hastati, principes, triarii), and improving cavalry and light infantry coordination. title.en: Battle of Pydna: Rome Annihilates Macedon

summary.en: At Pydna in northern Greece, the Roman consul Paullus faced King Perseus. The Roman legions exploited terrain to break the Macedonian phalanx's formation, then attacked its flanks. The Macedonian army disintegrated: 20,000 killed, 11,000 captured. Perseus surrendered and was later paraded in Rome and died in captivity. Macedon was divided into four republics, effectively Roman

statement.zh: 罗马执政官保卢斯与马其顿国王佩尔修斯在皮德纳（今希腊北部）决战。罗马军团利用地形迫使马其顿方阵无法保持队形，随后从侧翼突破。马其顿军崩溃，2万人被杀，1.1万人被俘，佩尔修斯投降后被囚禁罗马。马其顿被分为四个共和国，实际上成为罗马附庸。第三次马其顿战争结束。
statement.en:
At Pydna in northern Greece, the Roman consul Paullus faced King Perseus. The Roman legions exploited terrain to break the Macedonian phalanx's formation, then attacked its flanks. The Macedonian army disintegrated: 20,000 killed, 11,000 captured. Perseus surrendered and was later paraded in Rome and died in captivity. Macedon was divided into four republics, effectively Roman puppets. The Third Macedonian War was over.

For Europe in 168 BCE, “Battle of Pydna: Rome Annihilates Macedon” is a traceable node of Military change whose significance is best read through later events.

title.en: Maccabean Revolt Erupts

summary.en: The Jewish priest Mattathias killed a Seleucid official and fled into the desert. His son Judas Maccabeus ('The Hammer') took command. Using guerrilla tactics, the rebels captured villages around Jerusalem and ambushed Seleucid troops. Judas defeated General Apollonius at Mizpah, seizing weapons and equipment and greatly increasing his strength.

title.en: Death of Antiochus IV; Civil War in Seleucid Empire

summary.en: Antiochus IV died during a campaign in Persia. His nine‑year‑old son Antiochus V succeeded, with Lysias as regent. Soon several pretenders appeared: Demetrius I (son of Seleucus IV), who escaped from Rome as a hostage, returned and seized the throne. Civil war exhausted Seleucid strength, allowing the Maccabees to consolidate Jewish independence.

statement.zh: 安条克四世在远征波斯途中病逝，他九岁的儿子安条克五世即位，由大臣吕西阿斯摄政。但迅速出现多个篡位者：德米特里一世（塞琉古四世之子）从罗马作为人质逃回，夺回王位。内战耗尽了塞琉古国力，马加比趁机巩固犹太独立。

Antiochus IV died during a campaign in Persia. His nine‑year‑old son Antiochus V succeeded, with Lysias as regent. title.en: Emperor Wen Abolishes Land Tax

summary.en: Emperor Wen decreed a complete abolition of the land tax for the whole empire, lasting for eleven years (163–155 BCE). This was the first long‑term land‑tax remission in Chinese history. Combined with the previous low rate of one‑thirtieth, it greatly stimulated agriculture. The state treasury became so full that 'grain stored in the capital's granaries rotted from age.'

statement.zh: 马尔库斯·波尔基乌斯·加图（老加图）逝世，终年85岁。他是罗马著名的保守派政治家、演说家和作家，著《农业志》，极力反对希腊文化侵蚀，提倡传统罗马美德，名言“迦太基必须毁灭”。他的曾孙小加图在罗马内战中成为元老院派领袖。
statement.en:
Marcus Porcius Cato (Cato the Elder) died at the age of about 85. He was a famous Roman conservative politician, orator, and writer. He wrote 'De Agri Cultura' and adamantly opposed Greek cultural influence, championing traditional Roman virtues. His famous phrase was 'Carthage must be destroyed.' His great‑grandson, Cato the Younger, became a leader of the senatorial faction during the Roman civil wars.

For Europe in 159 BCE, “Death of Cato the Elder” is a traceable node of Figure change whose significance is best read through later events.

title.en: Xiongnu raid the frontier; Zhou Yafu drills the camp at Xiliu

summary.en: In the winter of 158 BCE thirty thousand Xiongnu horsemen struck Shang commandery and another thirty thousand struck Yunzhong, and the beacon fires reached the approaches to Chang’an. Emperor Wen posted Zhou Yafu at Xiliu, Liu Li at Bashang and Xu Li at Jimen. Reviewing the troops, the emperor rode straight into the first two camps, but at Xiliu the gate stayed shut until an im

statement.zh: 文帝后元六年冬，匈奴三万骑入上郡、三万骑入云中，烽火直逼长安。文帝命周亚夫军细柳、刘礼军霸上、徐厉军棘门以备胡。文帝亲往劳军，霸上、棘门皆长驱直入，唯细柳营按军法闭壁拒门，须持节诏令方得入，且军中不得驰驱。文帝叹曰“此真将军矣”。匈奴旋即退兵，汉廷复行和亲。
statement.en:
In the winter of 158 BCE 30,000 Xiongnu horsemen struck Shang commandery and another 30,000 struck Yunzhong, and the beacon fires reached the approaches to Chang’an. Emperor Wen posted Zhou Yafu at Xiliu, Liu Li at Bashang and Xu Li at Jimen. Reviewing the troops, the emperor rode straight into the first two camps, but at Xiliu the gate stayed shut until an imperial credential was produced, and no one was allowed to gallop inside. “This,” said Emperor Wen, “is a true general.” The Xiongnu soon withdrew and the heqin marriage alliance was renewed.

For Asia in 158 BCE, “Xiongnu raid the frontier; Zhou Yafu drills the camp at Xiliu” is a traceable node of Military change whose significance is best read through later events.

title.en: Emperor Wen of Han Dies; Emperor Jing Ascends

summary.en: Emperor Wen of Han died. His heir Liu Qi ascended as Emperor Jing of Han. Jing continued Wen's policies of letting the people rest and employed Chao Cuo to implement the 'reduction of feudal kingdoms,' which led to the Rebellion of the Seven States (154 BCE). statement.zh: 汉文帝刘恒去世，太子刘启即位，是为汉景帝。景帝继续执行文帝休养生息政策，并重用晁错进行削藩，导致七国之乱（前154年）。文帝在位23年，与其子景帝统治时期被称为“文景之治”，是中国历史上第一个盛世。

Emperor Wen of Han died. His heir Liu Qi ascended as Emperor Jing of Han. Emperor Wen's 23‑year reign, together with his son Jing's, is known as the 'Rule of Wen and Jing'—the first golden age in Chinese imperial history.

title.en: Han Maintains Heqin and Border Markets with Xiongnu

summary.en: Emperor Jing continued the heqin policy and opened border markets (guan shi), allowing mutual trade. Through the markets, the Xiongnu obtained Han ironware, grain, and silk, temporarily reducing large‑scale incursions. However, small‑scale raids continued.

title.en: Hellenistic Philosopher Carneades Lectures in Rome

summary.en: The Greek philosopher Carneades (of the Academic Skeptical school) visited Rome as an envoy and gave public speeches on two consecutive days. On the first day he argued that justice is necessary and natural; on the second, with equal rhetorical skill, he refuted that argument, claiming that justice is merely a human convention. His cleverness enthralled Roman youths, but Cato t

statement.zh: 希腊哲学家卡尔内亚得（学园派怀疑论）作为使节访问罗马，连续两天作公开演讲：第一天论证正义是必要且自然产生的；第二天用同样的雄辩技巧推翻前一天的论点，说明正义只是人为约定。他的诡辩令罗马青年倾倒，但老加图极为愤怒，要求元老院遣返他，以防败坏传统道德。
statement.en:
The Greek philosopher Carneades (of the Academic Skeptical school) visited Rome as an envoy and gave public speeches on two consecutive days. On the first day he argued that justice is necessary and natural; on the second, with equal rhetorical skill, he refuted that argument, claiming that justice is merely a human convention. His cleverness enthralled Roman youths, but Cato the Elder was furious and demanded the Senate send him away to avoid corrupting traditional morality.

For Europe in 156 BCE, “Hellenistic Philosopher Carneades Lectures in Rome” is a traceable node of Culture change whose significance is best read through later events.

title.en: Numantian War in Spain

summary.en: Roman forces besieged the city of Numantia in Spain, but faced fierce resistance from the Celtiberians. The Roman consul Marcus Marcellus was forced to sign a humiliating treaty, which the Senate refused to ratify and instead sent more troops. The Numantian War lasted until 133 BCE, when Scipio Aemilianus finally took the city.

title.en: Chao Cuo Proposes 'Policy of Reducing Feudal Kingdoms'

summary.en: Censor‑in‑Chief Chao Cuo submitted a memorial to Emperor Jing listing the crimes of the vassal kings, notably Liu Bi of Wu, and advised reducing their territories. He argued: 'If we reduce them, they will rebel; if we don't reduce them, they will also rebel. Reducing them means a quicker rebellion but with smaller harm; delaying reduction makes the rebellion later but greater.'

statement.zh: 御史大夫晁错向景帝上《削藩策》，列举吴王刘濞等诸侯王的罪行，建议削夺其封地。他指出：“今削之亦反，不削之亦反。削之，其反亟，祸小；不削之，反迟，祸大。”景帝采纳，先后削夺楚、赵、胶西等国的部分郡县，直接引发了七国之乱。
statement.en:
Censor‑in‑Chief Chao Cuo submitted a memorial to Emperor Jing listing the crimes of the vassal kings, notably Liu Bi of Wu, and advised reducing their territories. He argued: 'If we reduce them, they will rebel; if we don't reduce them, they will also rebel. Reducing them means a quicker rebellion but with smaller harm; delaying reduction makes the rebellion later but greater.' Jing accepted, and began taking counties from Chu, Zhao, Jiaoxi, and others, directly triggering the Rebellion of the Seven States.

For Asia in 155 BCE, “Chao Cuo Proposes 'Policy of Reducing Feudal Kingdoms'” is a traceable node of Politics change whose significance is best read through later events.

title.en: Construction Begins on Rome's First Stone Theater

summary.en: The Roman censor Marcus Aemilius Lepidus approved the construction of a permanent stone theater, but due to conservative opposition (who believed theater would corrupt morals), the building was never finished and was dismantled. Thereafter Roman theaters remained mostly wooden until the Theater of Pompey (55 BCE), the first permanent stone theater in Rome.

statement.en:
Liu Bi, King of Wu, led six other princes—Liu Wu of Chu, Liu Sui of Zhao, Liu Biguang of Jinan, Liu Xian of Zichuan, Liu Ang of Jiaoxi, and Liu Xiongqu of Jiaodong—in rebellion under the slogan 'kill Chao Cuo and purge the emperor's side.' The king of Wu mobilized over 200,000 troops and crossed the Huai River westwards. On the advice of Yuan Ang, Emperor Jing ordered the waist execution of Chao Cuo, but the rebels would not retreat. Jing then appointed Zhou Yafu and Dou Ying to suppress the rebellion, which was quelled after three months.

title.en: Rome Suppresses Lusitanian Revolt in Spain

summary.en: The Lusitanian (modern Portugal) leader Viriatus led a revolt and repeatedly defeated Roman forces using guerrilla tactics, attacking supply lines and bogging down the Romans. Rome was eventually forced to recognize his territory, but soon broke the treaty and assassinated Viriatus.

statement.zh: 卢西塔尼亚（今葡萄牙）领袖维里亚图斯（Viriatus）领导起义，屡败罗马军队。他采用游击战术，袭击罗马补给线，使罗马陷入苦战。罗马最终被迫承认其统治区域，但很快撕毁和约，暗杀维里亚图斯。
statement.en:
The Lusitanian (modern Portugal) leader Viriatus led a revolt and repeatedly defeated Roman forces using guerrilla tactics, attacking supply lines and bogging down the Romans. Rome was eventually forced to recognize his territory, but soon broke the treaty and assassinated Viriatus.

For Europe in 154 BCE, “Rome Suppresses Lusitanian Revolt in Spain” is a traceable node of Military change whose significance is best read through later events.

title.en: Rome Reforms Consular Term Dates

summary.en: The Roman Senate passed a law moving the start of the consular year from March 15 to January 1, to better coordinate military campaigns. title.en: Seleucid King Demetrius I Overthrown

summary.en: Civil war in the Seleucid Empire: Alexander Balas (claiming to be a son of Antiochus IV), supported by Pergamon and Egypt, seized the throne and killed Demetrius I. title.en: Hipparchus Founds Positional Astronomy

summary.en: The Greek astronomer Hipparchus (c. 190–120 BCE), observing from Rhodes, compiled a star catalog of 850 stars with positions and magnitudes. title.en: Third Punic War: Romans Begin Siege of Carthage

summary.en: Roman consuls Manius Manilius and Lucius Marcius Censorinus landed in Africa with about 80,000 troops and encamped outside Carthage. Inside, around 300,000 inhabitants—including women and slaves—worked feverishly to defend the city, tearing down buildings for timber and stone, and manufacturing weapons day and night. The Roman assault met fierce resistance.

statement.zh: 罗马执政官曼尼乌斯·马尼利乌斯和卢基乌斯·马尔基乌斯·肯索里努斯率领约8万军队渡过非洲，在迦太基城外扎营。迦太基城内约30万居民，包括妇女和奴隶，全部投入防御。他们拆除房屋的木材和石材制造武器，在城内设立工厂日夜生产弓箭和弹射器。罗马攻城遭遇顽强抵抗。
statement.en:
Roman consuls Manius Manilius and Lucius Marcius Censorinus landed in Africa with about 80,000 troops and encamped outside Carthage. Inside, around 300,000 inhabitants—including women and slaves—worked feverishly to defend the city, tearing down buildings for timber and stone, and manufacturing weapons day and night. The Roman assault met fierce resistance.

summary.en: After Scipio Aemilianus (Scipio Africanus the Younger) took command, he blockaded the harbor and built a mole reaching the city walls. summary.en: Emperor Jing ordered that the vassal kings could no longer personally administer their states. Instead, centrally appointed chancellors were to take full charge. The kings lost the power to appoint officials and collect taxes, retaining only the revenues from their domains. The principalities became administratively equivalent to commanderies, greatly strengthening central powe

statement.zh: 景帝下令诸侯王不得亲自治理封国，改由中央任命的“国相”全权负责；取消诸侯王的任命官吏权、征收赋税权，仅保留租税收入。诸侯国变成郡县一样的地方行政单位，中央集权空前加强。
statement.en:
Emperor Jing ordered that the vassal kings could no longer personally administer their states. Instead, centrally appointed chancellors were to take full charge. The kings lost the power to appoint officials and collect taxes, retaining only the revenues from their domains. The principalities became administratively equivalent to commanderies, greatly strengthening central power.

For Asia in 147 BCE, “Further Weakening of Vassal Kings After the Rebellion” is a traceable node of Politics change whose significance is best read through later events.

title.en: Carthage Razed to the Ground

summary.en: The Romans took full possession of Carthage. Scipio Aemilianus ordered the city burned; the fire lasted 17 days. The city was leveled and plowed over (traditionally with salt sown as a curse). The surviving 50,000 Carthaginians were sold into slavery, and Carthaginian territory became the Roman province of Africa. Thus ended the Third Punic War; Carthage ceased to exist as a st

statement.zh: 罗马军队完全占领迦太基，小西庇阿下令焚烧全城，大火持续17天。城市化为废墟，罗马人将其铲平并在土地上撒盐（象征诅咒）。幸存的5万迦太基人被卖为奴隶，迦太基领土成为罗马的阿非利加行省。至此，第三次布匿战争结束，迦太基作为国家不复存在。
statement.en:
The Romans took full possession of Carthage. Scipio Aemilianus ordered the city burned; the fire lasted 17 days. The city was leveled and plowed over (traditionally with salt sown as a curse). The surviving 50,000 Carthaginians were sold into slavery, and Carthaginian territory became the Roman province of Africa. Thus ended the Third Punic War; Carthage ceased to exist as a state.

For Africa in 146 BCE, “Carthage Razed to the Ground” is a traceable node of Military change whose significance is best read through later events.

罗马军队完全占领迦太基，小西庇阿下令焚烧全城，大火持续17天。
en: The Romans took full possession of Carthage. Scipio Aemilianus ordered the city burned; the fire lasted 17 days. The city was leveled and plowed over (traditionally with salt sown as a curse). The surviving 50,000 Carthaginians were sold into slavery, and Carthaginian territory became the Roman province of Africa. Thus ended the Third Punic War; Carthage ceased to exist as a state.

title.en: Rome Destroys Corinth; Greece Fully Annexed

summary.en: Rome crushed the revolt of the Achaean League. The consul Lucius Mummius captured and burned Corinth, slaughtering the adult males and selling the women and children into slavery. Greece was incorporated into the province of Macedonia (later Achaea was separated). The political independence of ancient Greek civilization ended.

title.en: Rome Builds the First Aqueduct (Aqua Marcia)

summary.en: The Roman praetor Marcus Marcius oversaw construction of the first stone aqueduct, Aqua Marcia, about 91 km long, of which some 80 km were underground, bringing water from the Anio River to Rome. It used numerous arches; parts still survive.

title.en: Min Yue Attacks Dongyue; Emperor Wu Sends Relief

summary.en: The king of Min Yue attacked Dongyue (modern Wenzhou, Zhejiang). Dongyue appealed to the Han for help. Emperor Wu sent Yan Zhu with naval forces from Kuaiji; before they arrived, Min Yue withdrew. statement.zh: 闽越王郢发兵攻打东瓯（今浙江温州），东瓯向汉朝求救。汉武帝派严助率会稽水军从海路救援，兵未至而闽越已退。东瓯王请求举国内迁，武帝将其安置在江淮之间。这是汉朝首次干预东南越人事务。
statement.en:
The king of Min Yue attacked Dongyue (modern Wenzhou, Zhejiang). Dongyue appealed to the Han for help. Emperor Wu sent Yan Zhu with naval forces from Kuaiji; before they arrived, Min Yue withdrew. The Dongyue king asked to move his people inside China, and the Han settled them between the Yangtze and Huai rivers. This was the first Han military intervention in the southeast Yue peoples.

title.en: King Attalus III of Pergamon Dies, Bequeaths Kingdom to Rome

summary.en: Attalus III, king of Pergamon, died without an heir. In his will, he left the entire Pergamene kingdom to Rome. The Senate accepted, and in 129 BCE formalized the province of Asia. This shocked other Anatolian states and led to the rebellion of Aristonicus, a pretender to the Pergamene throne.

statement.zh: 帕加马国王阿塔罗斯三世去世，无子嗣，遗嘱将整个帕加马王国赠予罗马。罗马元老院接受，并于前129年正式设立亚细亚行省。这一事件引起小亚细亚其它国家的震动，也导致帕加马王位觊觎者阿里斯东尼克的叛乱。
statement.en:
Attalus III, king of Pergamon, died without an heir. In his will, he left the entire Pergamene kingdom to Rome. The Senate accepted, and in 129 BCE formalized the province of Asia. This shocked other Anatolian states and led to the rebellion of Aristonicus, a pretender to the Pergamene throne.

For Asia in 136 BCE, “King Attalus III of Pergamon Dies, Bequeaths Kingdom to Rome” is a traceable node of Politics change whose significance is best read through later events.

title.en: Tiberius Gracchus Elected Tribune

summary.en: Tiberius Gracchus was elected tribune of the plebs. He proposed land reform limiting the amount of public land (ager publicus) that wealthy individuals could hold and distributing the surplus to landless peasants. The Senate strongly opposed him; he bypassed the Senate and took the bill directly to the People's Assembly, setting a precedent for tribunes defying the Senate.

statement.zh: 提比略·格拉古当选保民官，提出土地改革法案，限制贵族占有公有地（Ager publicus）的数量，将多余土地分给无地农民。法案遭到元老院强烈反对，格拉古绕过元老院直接提交公民大会通过，开创了保民官与元老院对抗的先例。

title.en: Tiberius Gracchus Killed, Reform Fails

summary.en: Seeking re‑election as tribune, Tiberius Gracchus was accused of seeking tyranny. Senators and their clients attacked a public assembly, killing Gracchus and about 300 of his supporters, throwing their bodies into the Tiber. Gracchus's death inaugurated the era of civil violence in the late Roman Republic; political murder became normal.

title.en: Yellow River Breaks at Huzi; Major Flood Control Works

summary.en: The Yellow River broke its banks at Huzi (modern Puyang, Henan), flooding sixteen commanderies. Emperor Wu dispatched Ji An and Zheng Dangshi to repair the breach, but because the flood was so powerful, they repeatedly failed. It was not until 109 BCE (Yuanfeng 2) that the emperor personally visited the site and succeeded in plugging the gap.

statement.zh: 黄河在瓠子（今河南濮阳）决口，洪水泛滥十六郡。武帝派汲黯、郑当时主持堵口，但因水势太大屡次失败。直到前109年（元封2年）武帝亲临工地，才成功堵塞决口。
statement.en:
The Yellow River broke its banks at Huzi (modern Puyang, Henan), flooding sixteen commanderies. Emperor Wu dispatched Ji An and Zheng Dangshi to repair the breach, but because the flood was so powerful, they repeatedly failed. It was not until 109 BCE (Yuanfeng 2) that the emperor personally visited the site and succeeded in plugging the gap.

For Asia in 132 BCE, “Yellow River Breaks at Huzi; Major Flood Control Works” is a traceable node of Engineering change whose significance is best read through later events.

title.en: Rome Crushes the Sicilian Slave Revolt

summary.en: The Roman consul Publius Rupilius besieged the last rebel stronghold at Tauromenium (Taormina) and forced its surrender by starvation. The rebel leader Eunus was captured and died in prison. The Romans executed thousands of captured slaves. The First Sicilian Slave Revolt ended.

title.en: Han Reforms Currency, Issues San Guan Coins

summary.en: Because private coin‑minting was rampant, Emperor Wu banned minting by the commanderies and kingdoms, and instead had the three bureaus of the Shanglin Park (the Official of the Clock, the Assayer, and the Transport) uniformly cast 'five‑zhu' coins (wuzhu qian). These high‑quality, uniform coins became the standard currency of the Han dynasty for centuries.

title.en: Han's First Large‑Scale Sortie Against Xiongnu: Four Columns

summary.en: Emperor Wu ordered Wei Qing, General of Chariots and Cavalry, out of Shanggu; Gongsun Ao, General of Cavalry, out of Dai; Gongsun He, General of Light Chariots, out of Yunzhong; and Li Guang, General of Swift Cavalry, out of Yanmen, each with 10,000 horsemen. Wei Qing struck as far as the Longcheng, beheading 700. Li Guang encountered the main Xiongnu force, was captured, then

statement.zh: 武帝令车骑将军卫青出上谷，骑将军公孙敖出代郡，轻车将军公孙贺出云中，骁骑将军李广出雁门，各率万骑出击匈奴。卫青直捣龙城，斩首700级；李广遭遇匈奴主力被俘，后逃回；公孙敖损失七千骑；公孙贺无功。卫青因功封关内侯。
statement.en:
Emperor Wu ordered Wei Qing, General of Chariots and Cavalry, out of Shanggu; Gongsun Ao, General of Cavalry, out of Dai; Gongsun He, General of Light Chariots, out of Yunzhong; and Li Guang, General of Swift Cavalry, out of Yanmen, each with 10,000 horsemen. Wei Qing struck as far as the Longcheng, beheading 700. Li Guang encountered the main Xiongnu force, was captured, then escaped; Gongsun Ao lost 7,000 men; Gongsun He achieved nothing. Wei Qing was enfeoffed as Marquis of Guannei.

For Asia in 129 BCE, “Han's First Large‑Scale Sortie Against Xiongnu: Four Columns” is a traceable node of Military change whose significance is best read through later events.

title.en: Zhang Qian, Returning from Yuezhi, is Captured Again by Xiongnu

title.en: Gunchen Chanyu Dies; Yizhixie Usurps Throne

summary.en: Gunchen Chanyu died. His younger brother Yizhixie defeated the heir apparent, Yudan, and proclaimed himself chanyu. Yudan fled to the Han, and Emperor Wu enfeoffed him as Marquis of She'an. Yizhixie, after taking power, adopted a tougher stance toward the Han, with annual invasions.

statement.zh: 军臣单于死，其弟伊稚斜击败太子於丹，自立为单于；於丹逃奔汉朝，武帝封其为涉安侯。伊稚斜即位后，对汉朝采取更强硬的态度，连年入侵。兄弟取代太子，使单于继承从父死子继转向以实力争夺；於丹投汉并获得封号，则把匈奴内部争端带入汉匈关系，为后来的边境冲突提供了直接背景。
statement.en: Gunchen Chanyu died.

title.en: Zhang Qian Accompanying Wei Qing, Suggests New Missions to Western Regions

summary.en: Zhang Qian accompanied Wei Qing as a colonel; because of his geographical knowledge, he found water and grass for the army, earning the title of Marquis of Bowang. He advised the emperor to send more missions to the Western Regions to 'cut off the Xiongnu's right arm.' Emperor Wu accepted, and Zhang Qian set out on his second mission in 119 BCE.

Zhang Qian accompanied Wei Qing as a colonel; because of his geographical knowledge, he found water and grass for the army, earning the title of Marquis of Bowang. title.en: Emperor Wu of Han establishes the Imperial Academy

summary.en: Emperor Wu of Han, following proposals of Dong Zhongshu and others, establishes the Imperial Academy (Taixue) with erudite students, inaugurating China's state higher learning.

statement.zh: 汉武帝采纳董仲舒等建议设立太学，置博士弟子员，开中国官办高等学府之先河。太学以儒家经典为教材，博士分经教授，学生经考核后进入仕途；官学与选官由此结合，使儒学成为国家治理与意识形态的重要载体。太学的建立也改变了知识传授的渠道，从私人讲学转向国家主导的教育机构。
statement.en: Emperor Wu of the Han Dynasty adopted the suggestions of Dong Zhongshu and others to establish Taixue and set up doctoral students, which was the first government-run higher education institution in China.

title.en: Wei Qing Twice Sorties from Dingxiang, Killing over 10,000

summary.en: Wei Qing led six generals on two sorties from Dingxiang, killing over 10,000 Xiongnu. However, two divisions under Su Jian and Zhao Xin were wiped out, and Zhao Xin, a former Xiongnu officer who had surrendered, defected back to the Xiongnu and became a key adviser to Yizhixie Chanyu.

The Xiongnu lamented, 'Lost our Qilian Mountains, our six animals will not multiply; lost our Yanzhi Mountains, our women have no faces.'

title.en: Emperor Wu Centralizes Minting, Issues Wuzhu Coins

summary.en: Emperor Wu centralized coin‑minting authority under the three bureaus of the Shanglin Park, which cast uniform 'wuzhu' coins weighing five zhu (about 3.25 grams), with a raised rim to prevent clipping. The wuzhu coin was stable and remained in circulation until the Tang dynasty, over 700 years.

statement.zh: 武帝将铸币权收归中央，由上林三官统一铸造五铢钱，重五铢（约3.25克），周边加郭，防止磨铅。
statement.en: Emperor Wu centralized coin‑minting authority under the three bureaus of the Shanglin Park, which cast uniform 'wuzhu' coins weighing five zhu (about 3.25 grams), with a raised rim to prevent clipping.

zh: 武帝将铸币权收归中央，由上林三官统一铸造五铢钱，重五铢（约3.25克），周边加郭，防止磨铅。
en: Emperor Wu centralized coin‑minting authority under the three bureaus of the Shanglin Park, which cast uniform 'wuzhu' coins weighing five zhu (about 3.25 grams), with a raised rim to prevent clipping.

title.en: Huo Qubing Dies Young

summary.en: Huo Qubing, only 24 years old, died. Emperor Wu was deeply grieved; he ordered the five commanderies to provide iron‑clad soldiers to line the funeral procession and had the tomb shaped like the Qilian Mountains. Huo had six campaigns against the Xiongnu, never tasted defeat, and was famous for his saying, 'Before the Xiongnu are destroyed, how can I have a home?'

title.en: Rome Establishes First Veteran Colonies

summary.en: Marius, to settle discharged veterans, founded colonies in Africa and Corsica, distributing land. This practice later became a common way for Roman generals to build private power bases.

statement.zh:
马略为安置退伍老兵，在非洲和科西嘉建立殖民地，分给土地。此举后来成为罗马将领培植私人势力的惯用手段。殖民地以土地分配换取兵役忠诚，老兵在行省定居并形成可动员的群体；将领借安置权扩大个人影响，削弱了元老院对军队的控制。

把「罗马建立第一座老兵殖民地」放回公元前117年的罗马共和国，可以看到政治变化的一个具体切面。

title.en: Han Establishes Jiuquan and Wuwei Commanderies

summary.en: In the Hexi Corridor, Han established Jiuquan and Wuwei commanderies, later adding Zhangye and Dunhuang, the 'Four Commanderies of Hexi.' These served as strategic bases to control the Western Regions, separate the Qiang, and protect the Silk Road.

statement.zh: 在河西走廊设立酒泉、武威二郡，后增设张掖、敦煌，合称河西四郡。这些郡县成为控制西域、隔绝羌胡、保护丝路的战略据点。
statement.en:
In the Hexi Corridor, Han established Jiuquan and Wuwei commanderies, later adding Zhangye and Dunhuang, the 'Four Commanderies of Hexi.' These served as strategic bases to control the Western Regions, separate the Qiang, and protect the Silk Road.

For Asia in 117 BCE, “Han Establishes Jiuquan and Wuwei Commanderies” is a traceable node of Politics change whose significance is best read through later events.

title.en: Jugurthine War Enters Critical Phase

summary.en: The Roman consul Metellus scored some successes in Numidia but failed to capture Jugurtha. Jugurtha exploited Roman generals' corruption and indecision to escape repeatedly. Frustrated by the war's delay, the Senate transferred command to Marius.

title.en: Zhang Qian Returns from Wusun; Wusun Envoys Accompany Him

summary.en: Zhang Qian, unable to persuade the Wusun to move east, returned to Chang'an accompanied by several dozen Wusun envoys. The envoys saw Han power and, after reporting back, the Wusun began to take relations with the Han seriously. Zhang Qian died soon thereafter, but the Han passage to the Western Regions was permanently opened.

summary.en: Sulla, serving as Marius's legate in the Jugurthine War, used diplomacy to trick King Jugurtha into surrendering (105 BCE). He led Jugurtha to believe he would be lenient, then handed him over to the Romans. Sulla began to gain political prestige.

title.en: Han Formally Establishes Trade Relations with Western States

summary.en: Building on Zhang Qian's foundations, the Han established official trade ties with Wusun, Dayuan, Bactria, Parthia, and others. title.en: Civil War in Nanyue; Han Intervenes

summary.en: The king of Nanyue, Zhao Xing, and his mother, the queen dowager Jiu ( Jiu ), supported incorporation into the Han, but the chancellor Lü Jia opposed them and staged a coup, killing Zhao Xing and the queen dowager. Emperor Wu ordered Lu Bode and others to lead a punitive expedition.

statement.zh:
南越王赵兴和太后樛氏主张内属汉朝，但丞相吕嘉反对并发动政变，杀死赵兴和樛氏。汉武帝派路博德等率兵征讨。内属之争实质是南越亲汉与本土势力的角力，吕嘉依托越人贵族与地方军队夺权；汉廷则以平乱为名推进统一。南越的独立地位由此终结。

把「南越国内乱，汉朝出兵」放回公元前113年的南越国，可以看到军事变化的一个具体切面。

title.en: Jugurthine War Ends

summary.en: Marius defeated Jugurtha's Moorish allies, isolating Jugurtha. Sulla arranged his capture and handed him over to Rome. Jugurtha was condemned to death and died in the Mamertine prison. Rome established the province of Africa to administer Numidia.

title.en: Han Conquers Nanyue, Establishes Nine Commanderies

summary.en: Han generals Lu Bode and Yang Pu, with naval and land forces, captured the Nanyue capital Panyu, killing Lü Jia. Nanyue was extinguished, and the Han established nine commanderies: Nanhai, Cangwu, Yulin, Hepu, Jiaozhi, Jiuzhen, Rinan, Zhuya, and Dan'er, bringing the Lingnan region formally into the empire.

statement.zh: 汉将路博德、杨仆率水陆大军攻破南越都城番禺，擒杀吕嘉。

title.en: Rome Defeated by Cimbri at Arausio

summary.en: The Roman consul Caepio was defeated at Arausio (modern Orange, France) by the Cimbri, losing about 80,000 men. The Senate urgently recalled Marius to lead the army north.

statement.zh:
罗马执政官卡波在阿劳西奥（今法国）与辛布里人交战，惨败，损失约8万军队。罗马元老院急令马略率军北上。两军指挥不统一、地形不利，罗马阵线被突破，损失惨重；败报震动了罗马，元老院遂把北方的指挥权交给马略。此役成为共和国军事改革的导火索之一。

把「罗马战败辛布里人和条顿人于阿劳西奥」放回公元前111年的罗马共和国，可以看到军事变化的一个具体切面。

title.en: Zhao Guo invents the seed drill

summary.en: The Han agricultural official Zhao Guo devised the louche, a three-pipe seed drill that opened furrows, sowed and covered in one pass.

statement.zh:
西汉农官赵过改进农具，创制耧车（三脚播种机），实现开沟、下种、覆土一次完成。耧车以畜力牵引，三足分别开沟漏种，行距与播深较手工撒播均匀，省种省工；赵过推广时配套代田法，使耕作与农具相互配合。这一农具在北方旱作区长期沿用。

把「赵过创制耧车」放回公元前110年的中国，可以看到农业变化的一个具体切面。

title.en: Han Campaign Against Gojoseon (Korea)

summary.en: Wiman Joseon's king Ugeo ( Ugeo ) prevented smaller states from communicating with the Han and killed Han envoys. Emperor Wu sent the naval commander Yang Pu and the army commander Xun Zhi with 50,000 troops to attack.

title.en: Marius recruits the landless and the legion moves toward professionalization

summary.en: Traditional accounts treat 107 BCE as the starting point of the Marian reform. Elected consul at the end of 108 and taking office in 107, Marius recruited landless volunteers because the Numidian war lacked manpower; this broke the property-owner tradition and pushed the legion toward professionalization.

statement.zh: 传统叙述把前107年当作马略军改的起点。前108年末，马略当选执政官；前107年上任后，他在努米底亚战争中因兵源不足，开始征募没有财产资格的志愿者。
statement.en: Traditional accounts treat 107 BCE as the starting point of the Marian reform. At the end of 108 Marius was elected consul; after taking office in 107, short of manpower in the Numidian war, he began recruiting volunteers without the property qualification.

sources.excerpt: Gaius Marius (c. 157–86 BCE) was a Roman general and politician who served as consul seven times.

sources.locator: Britannica, Gaius Marius, section 'Election to the consulship'
sources.excerpt: In recruiting fresh troops, Marius broke with custom, because of a manpower shortage, by enrolling volunteers from outside the propertied classes, which alone had previously been liable for service.

zh: 传统叙述把前107年当作马略军改的起点。
前108年末，马略当选执政官；前107年上任后，他在努米底亚战争中因兵源不足，开始征募没有财产资格的志愿者。
en: Traditional accounts treat 107 BCE as the starting point of the Marian reform.
At the end of 108 Marius was elected consul; after taking office in 107, short of manpower in the Numidian war, he began recruiting volunteers without the property qualification.

note.zh: 前107为传统起点；不写“一次法令完成全部军改”。
note.en: 107 BCE is the traditional starting point; no single law completed the whole reform.

statement.zh: 这打破了此前只有有产者承担兵役的惯例。无产者参军，使军队规模不再完全受财产门槛限制，也让服役越来越成为一份长期职业。
statement.en: This broke the previous rule that only property owners were liable for service. Landless soldiers widened recruitment beyond the property threshold and made service increasingly a long-term career.

sources.locator: Britannica, Gaius Marius, section 'Election to the consulship'
sources.excerpt: In recruiting fresh troops, Marius broke with custom, because of a manpower shortage, by enrolling volunteers from outside the propertied classes, which alone had previously been liable for service.

sources.locator: Britannica, Gaius Marius, top question 'What role did Gaius Marius play in the Roman army?'
sources.excerpt: This created a professional army more loyal to its general than to the state, with far-reaching political consequences.

zh: 这打破了此前只有有产者承担兵役的惯例。
无产者参军，使军队规模不再完全受财产门槛限制，也让服役越来越成为一份长期职业。
en: This broke the previous rule that only property owners were liable for service.
Landless soldiers widened recruitment beyond the property threshold and made service increasingly a long-term career.

note.zh: 兵源不足是因，募兵范围扩大是果；职业化是长期后果。
note.en: Manpower shortage is the cause, wider recruitment the result; professionalization is the long-term consequence.

statement.zh: 马略还强化了军团鹰旗的象征作用，提升了大队作为战术单位的地位。
statement.en: Marius also strengthened the legionary eagle as a standard and raised the cohort's importance as a tactical unit.

sources.locator: Britannica, Gaius Marius, top question 'What role did Gaius Marius play in the Roman army?'
sources.excerpt: He also enhanced the importance of the legionary eagle as the standard, fostering a stronger corporate identity within each legion.

sources.locator: Britannica, Gaius Marius, top question 'What role did Gaius Marius play in the Roman army?'
sources.excerpt: Additionally, Marius' tactical reforms led to the increasing prominence of the cohort as a tactical unit.

zh: 马略还强化了军团鹰旗的象征作用，提升了大队作为战术单位的地位。
en: Marius also strengthened the legionary eagle as a standard and raised the cohort's importance as a tactical unit.

note.zh: 鹰旗与大队战术；不写“每军团10个大队、每大队6个百人队”的精确编制。
note.en: Eagle and cohort tactics; no exact 10-cohort/6-century table is asserted.

statement.zh: 职业化解决了兵源，也改变了忠诚结构。
statement.en: Professionalization solved the manpower problem and changed the structure of loyalty.

sources.locator: Britannica, Gaius Marius, top question 'What role did Gaius Marius play in the Roman army?'
sources.excerpt: This created a professional army more loyal to its general than to the state, with far-reaching political consequences.

zh: 职业化解决了兵源，也改变了忠诚结构。
en: Professionalization solved the manpower problem and changed the structure of loyalty.

note.zh: 职业化改变忠诚结构，是条目的判断。
note.en: The entry itself links professionalization to a change in loyalty.

statement.zh: 老兵退役后要土地、要军饷，越来越依赖将军兑现；马略的退伍兵在政治上支持他，苏拉、凯撒与屋大维后来把这种力量用到极致。
statement.en: Veterans wanted land and pay after discharge and depended increasingly on generals to deliver; Marius's veterans supported him politically, and Sulla, Caesar and Octavian later used that force to the full.

sources.excerpt: Marius was the first Roman to illustrate the political support that a successful general could derive from the votes of his old army veterans.

zh: 老兵退役后要土地、要军饷，越来越依赖将军兑现；马略的退伍兵在政治上支持他，苏拉、凯撒与屋大维后来把这种力量用到极致。
en: Veterans wanted land and pay after discharge and depended increasingly on generals to deliver; Marius's veterans supported him politically, and Sulla, Caesar and Octavian later used that force to the full.

note.zh: 退伍兵的政治支持照条目写；不写“士兵只认将军、完全不认国家”。
note.en: Veterans' political support follows the entry; no absolute 'soldiers knew only their general'.

statement.zh: 这些变化不是一部法令在一天内完成的，而是长期累积；后来帝国军团的编制，常被追溯到这一过程。
statement.en: These changes were not a single statute completed in one day but a long accumulation; the later imperial legion is often traced back to this process.

zh: 这些变化不是一部法令在一天内完成的，而是长期累积；后来帝国军团的编制，常被追溯到这一过程。
en: These changes were not a single statute completed in one day but a long accumulation; the later imperial legion is often traced back to this process.

note.zh: 作者判断：军改是长期累积，不能压缩成107年的单日制度。
note.en: Author judgment: the reform was cumulative and cannot be reduced to a single day in 107.

title.en: Han Destroys Wiman Joseon, Establishes Four Commanderies

summary.en: The Han army took the capital Wanggeomseong (Pyongyang), killed King Ugeo, and ended Wiman Joseon. The Han set up the commanderies of Lelang, Xuantu, Lintun, and Zhenfan, bringing the northern Korean Peninsula into the empire.

statement.zh:
汉军攻陷王险城（平壤），卫右渠被杀，卫氏朝鲜亡。汉朝在其地设乐浪、玄菟、临屯、真番四郡，将朝鲜半岛北部纳入版图。设郡把当地政权纳入汉的官僚与礼制，移民、屯田与商路随之进入；地方部族的反抗时有发生。东北亚的政治格局由此改变。

把「汉朝灭亡卫氏朝鲜，设立汉四郡」放回公元前108年的西汉，可以看到政治变化的一个具体切面。
statement.en: The Han army took the capital Wanggeomseong, present-day Pyongyang, killed King Ugeo and ended Wiman Joseon.

title.en: Han and Parthia Exchange Official Missions

summary.en: The Parthian king Mithradates II sent an envoy to Chang'an, presenting large bird eggs and jugglers from Liqian (Roman territory). The Han reciprocated, sending envoys to Parthia, and diplomatic relations were established. The western Silk Road became more secure.

statement.zh:

title.en: Birth of Cicero

title.en: Emperor Wu Promulgates the 'Taichu Calendar'

summary.en: Emperor Wu ordered Luoxiahong and Deng Ping to reform the calendar, issuing the Taichu Calendar, which set the first month as the beginning of the year, adopted the Xia calendar, and for the first time incorporated the 24 solar terms into the lunisolar calendar. The Taichu Calendar was the first complete, fully documented calendar in Chinese history.

title.en: Marius Defeats the Teutones at Aquae Sextiae

summary.en: Marius ambushed the Teutones in a valley near Aquae Sextiae, annihilating their main force. The Teutones lost about 90,000 men, and their king was captured. Rome seized vast booty.

statement.zh:
马略在普罗旺斯附近的山谷中伏击条顿人，全歼其主力。条顿人损失约9万人，国王被俘。罗马缴获大量战利品。马略选择谷地设伏，待敌军通过时从两侧夹击，使其阵形崩溃；战后俘虏与战利品被用于凯旋与安置。此役与对辛布里人的胜利，稳住了罗马的北方边境。

title.en: Han Army Captures Dayuan, Obtains 'Heavenly Horses'

summary.en: Li Guangli besieged the Dayuan capital, Guishan, for over 40 days. Dayuan nobles killed their king, Mugu, and offered horses. The Han selected several dozen fine horses and over 3,000 medium horses for the return to Chang'an. Li Guangli was enfeoffed as Marquis of Haixi. Dayuan submitted; the Western states trembled and sent hostages.

Li Guangli besieged the Dayuan capital, Guishan, for over 40 days. Dayuan nobles killed their king, Mugu, and offered horses. title.en: Han Sets Up Prototype of the Western Regions Protectorate

title.en: Western Han Imperial Academy Expands

summary.en: During Emperor Wu's reign, the Imperial Academy was established in Chang'an, where Erudites of the Five Classics taught Confucian texts. Initially enrolling 50 students, the numbers grew yearly. The Academy trained many civil officials for Han and promoted Confucianism as the state ideology. This state-run higher education system was inherited by later dynasties.

statement.zh: 汉武帝时期，西汉太学设在长安，由五经博士教授儒家经典，初设博士弟子五十人，此后逐年增加。太学为汉朝培养了大量文官人才，推动儒家思想成为国家官方意识形态。这一国家设立高等学府的教育体系为后世历代王朝所继承。
statement.en:
During Emperor Wu's reign, the Imperial Academy was established in Chang'an, where Erudites of the Five Classics taught Confucian texts. Initially enrolling 50 students, the numbers grew yearly. The Academy trained many civil officials for Han and promoted Confucianism as the state ideology. This state-run higher education system was inherited by later dynasties.

For Asia in 100 BCE, “Western Han Imperial Academy Expands” is a traceable node of Culture change whose significance is best read through later events.

title.en: Batik spreads in the southwest

summary.en: Wax-resist dyeing with bee's wax and indigo spread among ethnic groups of the southwest; its natural crackle patterns became a distinctive textile craft.

statement.zh:
以蜂蜡防染、蓝靛浸染的蜡染在西南少数民族中传承，冰纹自然，形成独特的民族纺织工艺。做法以蜡刀在布上绘纹，浸入蓝靛后蜡层阻染，去蜡后留下蓝白花纹，蜡的裂痕形成细碎的冰纹；纹样多取铜鼓、鸟兽与几何。技艺随族群迁徙而流布。

把「蜡染技艺流行于西南」放回公元前100年的中国，可以看到工艺变化的一个具体切面。

title.en: Mercury-gilding (liujin) matures in China

summary.en: In the Han dynasty the mercury-amalgam gilding method coated bronze with gold, producing fine gilt vessels and fittings and marking a major advance in metal ornament.

statement.zh:
汉代以汞剂鎏金法将金箔涂覆于铜器表面，鎏金青铜器与车马器精美，标志金属装饰工艺的重大进步。工艺把金与汞调成泥状涂布，再加热驱汞使金层附着，厚薄与打磨决定光泽；器物在礼制与日用中都显贵重。技术依赖对火候与毒气的控制。

把「中国鎏金工艺成熟」放回公元前100年的中国，可以看到工艺变化的一个具体切面。

title.en: The oasis city of Merv

summary.en: Merv in Central Asia was a great oasis city between Parthia and Sogdiana, a thriving Silk Road hub of trade and Buddhism.

statement.zh:
中亚木鹿为安息与粟特间的绿洲大城，商旅辐辏，是丝绸之路上的重要贸易与佛教中心。城市依托穆尔加布河的灌溉绿洲，城墙、巴扎与寺院分区布置，商队在此补给并转输丝绸、金属与香料。佛教寺院与粟特商人的聚落并存，使木鹿成为宗教与商业交汇的节点。

summary.en: Emperor Wu sent Su Wu as envoy to the Xiongnu to escort Xiongnu envoys home and repair relations. When Su Wu prepared to return, internal strife erupted among the Xiongnu. statement.zh: 汉武帝派苏武以中郎将身份持节出使匈奴，目的是护送匈奴使者回国并修复汉匈关系。苏武完成使命准备回国时，匈奴发生内乱，副使张胜卷入谋反事件。匈奴单于扣留苏武并逼其投降，苏武坚称“屈节辱命，虽生何面目以归汉”，拔刀自刺被救下。单于将他流放到北海（贝加尔湖）边牧羊，声称公羊产羔才能放他回国。
statement.en:
Emperor Wu sent Su Wu as envoy to the Xiongnu to escort Xiongnu envoys home and repair relations. When Su Wu prepared to return, internal strife erupted among the Xiongnu. His deputy Zhang Sheng became implicated in a rebellion. The Xiongnu Chanyu detained Su Wu and demanded surrender. Su Wu declared, 'To betray my integrity and disgrace my mission - even alive, how could I face Han?' He attempted suicide but was rescued. The Chanyu exiled him to herd sheep by Lake Baikal, claiming he could only return when rams gave birth.

For Asia in 100 BCE, “Su Wu Sent as Envoy to Xiongnu” is a traceable node of Diplomacy change whose significance is best read through later events.

title.en: Rome masters volcanic-ash concrete

summary.en: Roman builders used pozzolana ash to make concrete, enabling domes and arches that transformed architecture.

statement.zh: 罗马工匠以火山灰（波佐利灰）配制混凝土，得以建造穹顶与拱券，革新建筑。火山灰与石灰、碎石混合后在水下也能硬化，使港口、拱券与穹顶获得更大的跨度与更强的整体性。材料与施工方法的结合，让罗马建筑摆脱对整块石材的依赖，在大型公共建筑中达到新的尺度。
statement.en: Roman craftsmen used volcanic ash (Pozzuoli ash) to prepare concrete and build domes and arches, revolutionizing architecture.

summary.en: Sericulture flourished on the Chengdu plain; Shu brocade, prized for vivid color and pattern, was traded far along both northern and southern Silk Roads.

statement.zh:
成都平原蚕桑兴盛，蜀锦以色彩绚丽、纹样华美著称，经南方与北方丝路远销，成为早期重要外贸商品。织造依赖桑蚕、染料与提花技术，锦工把经线与彩纬交织出云纹、瑞兽；蜀地的水源与气候适宜蚕桑。织品既是贡赋也是商品。

把「蜀锦闻名于世」放回公元前100年的中国，可以看到工艺变化的一个具体切面。
